summary: @factiii/runner ships a documented remote-agent daemon with WebRTC control plane and bundled frp tunnels
details: The package is a user-invoked daemon (`factiii-runner start`) that pairs with Factiii's web/mobile clients over WebRTC via api.factiii.com and runs AI coding agents (Claude/Codex) on the host, driven by the paired remote party. It also ships prebuilt `frpc` binaries (`vendor/frpc-{linux,darwin}-{amd64,arm64}`) that implement a documented `factiii-expose <port> <name>` capability publishing arbitrary local ports to the public internet, described in the README as a public unauthenticated URL. The remote-control and port-exposure capabilities are advertised as the product, require a pairing JWT (with optional password/2FA), store credentials in the OS keychain, and are not auto-started: there are no install lifecycle hooks and the daemon only runs when the operator launches the CLI. The traced capability matches what the README documents; no bulk credential or environment scraping, no install-time fetch-and-execute, and no hidden second channel are present. Residual concerns are the full-host blast radius intrinsic to a remote-agent runner, the ability to publish any local port over frp, and that the vendored frpc binaries were not independently verified against upstream fatedier/frp.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
